about: The record of the Job study2_calculate_v4: version 4 of the calculation tool and the lead developer's two revisions of it, version 4's commit, the check of the earlier paid runs for plain wildcard conditions, the debug against the stack, the fake-client dry run, the paid confirmation study2-confirm-v4-1 and the declared tool check run against the existing baseline study2-baseline-totals-1, with the lead developer's classification of the one failure and their verdict.

decisions.V1: (a) version 4 with one generic fix (an "any element" filter condition), then one more confirmation

version4.what: a filter condition may carry elements any or none: any holds when at least one value at its field satisfies the comparison, none when no value does; the values are found as a source path finds records (* takes every element of a list, a list at the end gives its elements, an element lacking the rest of the field is left out), so an empty list or a missing field has none; a condition whose field has a * path segment and no elements is refused ("Wildcard fields require elements: \"any\" or \"none\"."); a text on a condition's field that cannot be read as JSON or XML is refused; every other condition, the read line, the stored outputs, the view pages and every limit unchanged; manifest harnessTools version 4 with conditionElements
revisions: review finding P2 of the lead developer before the preview: field_values caught every CalculationError, so a text that could not be read (broken XML, a document type) was taken as a missing field; fixed with PathMissing for a missing path step only, and a list at the end of a condition's field read as * reads it, with a regression test

scope change by the lead developer before the preview: a condition whose field has a * path segment requires elements, the one deliberate exception to "existing conditions unchanged"; version 3 treated such a field as missing, which could silently include or exclude records depending on the comparison
two wording corrections of the lead developer (P3) to the design sentence on that exception, made before the go

toolCheck.declared: the tool is fit only if the failures where the agent says it cannot count and the failures from token volume fall, the definitional failures stay as they are, and no new kind of failure appears (a wrong operation or a wrong result id)
toolCheck.scope: V05 to V08 in beta, gamma, delta, epsilon, both models, one trial; the existing baseline study2-baseline-totals-1 (no tool) against study2-confirm-v4-1 (calculate version 4, commit 1c52d16), on the same pins; run 1, run 2, study2-confirm-1 and study2-confirm-v3-1 as history

tokenVolume.runs: confirm4: no run at or over 1 M, the largest 951 k (beta V05 Claude)

newKind.runs: confirm4 gamma V05 Claude: did_not_finish at the 80 tool-call limit (80 calls in 33 turns, 750,324 tokens, 139 s; 53 graphql_query and 27 calculate: 2 distinct, 4 union, 2 view, 1 group_by, 7 filter, 11 intersection). Two causes, as the lead developer classified them: a wrong operation that calculate accepted silently, and an inefficient strategy. Calls 71 to 77 were seven intersections, each with field personnelId, of 3932-62 (620 plain id values) with one rank's filtered records; because the first source holds plain values, not records with a personnelId field, each returned count 0 without a refusal, and the read line reported only "620 records" for that source. At call 78 the agent changed the second path to records.*.personnelId with no field and got real results (1, 69, 2 at calls 78 to 80); the run then stopped at the limit. The strategy: 53 graph queries against GPT's 20 in the same arm (GPT correct in 52 calls, 32 of them calculate, 0 refused). The one refused call (call 60, a union with path data.personnelReferences, no key data) was corrected at call 62, not the next call (call 61 was a different union). The run used no elements condition and no * field. The same run was correct with 75 calls in study2-confirm-v3-1

toolCheck.versionThreesFailure: delta V06 Claude, v3's one new kind, is correct in confirm4; 28 conditions with elements were used in 8 runs (every V06 run but beta V06 Claude, and beta V05 Claude); no call was refused for a wildcard field without elements
toolCheck.listFields: every graph query of the 24 graph-arm runs (gamma, delta, epsilon) parsed for its top-level fields: all 24 used missionsPage; none named the deprecated missions or assets lists, and none asked introspection with includeDeprecated. The parser's one hit, epsilon V06 Claude "assets", is Mission.assets inside a fragment (fragment F on Mission), checked by hand: the parser reads a fragment's fields as top-level ones
toolCheck.classifiedFrom: each failing run's transcript and results (calls, arguments, result sizes, refusals, read lines) and its outcome; the transcripts hold no model reasoning text. Scripts outside the repository: check4.py sha256 a2681c8901f8d3d84cb33cb36b7122c25a7dfb30582dd284ee78477dafbadc9d and fields4.py sha256 a150978ca43c2bb81404e58bf9264b541ca2d97643459afa83a31761b9c036b7, copies of check3.py and fields2.py with the new run
toolCheck.proposedVerdict: fails, on the new-kind clause (a stop at the tool-call limit, reached through a wrong operation repeated seven times); the limit question of entry 9 put beside it
verdictHistory: the lead developer first classified the stop as an agent-strategy limit stop, not a new kind, and, after the worker's two factual corrections (the refusal at call 60 corrected at call 62; the seven silent zeros at calls 71 to 77), selected "Yes, the check passes"
the lead developer then corrected the classification: "Under the declared check this is a new kind (a wrong operation). Record both causes." and selected "Yes, the check fails", replacing "passes"
toolCheck.decidedBy: the lead developer, in the worker session, 2026-11-05 (UTC), selected "Yes, the check fails"
toolCheck.consistency: this round counts a wrong operation that calculate accepted silently as a new kind, as version 3's round counted its filter on fixed list positions; version 2's round also counted epsilon V05 Claude, an incomplete fetch with no tool part, as a new kind
toolCheck.singleTrial: one trial of four tasks: one run moves each count
toolCheck.consequence: Under decision V4 (iii) the design returns to the lead developer, who decides then. Version 4 stays in the harness as committed (1c52d16); this Job changes it no further.
toolCheck.observation: the silent zero has the same shape as the wildcard case version 4 refuses: a field that does not apply to a source of plain values is read as missing (null), so a set operation with field over plain values compares nulls without a refusal (an intersection with real values then returns nothing). Not changed here; it is the lead developer's to decide

limitsForTheFreeze.decided: the lead developer: keep 80 calls, 1 M tokens, 900 s and 3 retries; "the limit did not cause the stop, the lost calls did". The largest run used 951 k tokens, the longest 416 s; calculate calls count toward the 80 (27 in the stopped run, 32 in GPT's correct one)
